correctness.rationale: For nonzero integers r,s, Cheng–Zhang Theorem 5.2 reduces PSI₃ of {r^[8],s} to rational squareness of (t−2)²+8 and 4t+5, t=s/r. q=u−(t−2)≠0, X=−2q, Y=2qv birationally give E:y²=x³+13x²−32x and t=(X²+8X−32)/(4X). E has two-isogenous E′:y²=x³−26x²+297x. Standard 2-isogeny descent: for E square-classes −1,2 impossible mod3 and 1,−2 present; E′ negative classes impossible over real numbers, positive 3,11 excluded mod16; positive classes 1,33 present. Thus each descent image size2 and rank zero. E has good reduction at 5,7, each with six points; six displayed rational points O,(0,0),(4,±12),(−8,±24) exhaust torsion and thus E(Q). Nonzero X maps only to t=1, giving s=r; converse all equal matrices has eigenvalues (3r,0,0). Independently checked modular obstructions, point counts and birational evaluations. No bounded search is used as proof of all Q-points.
